pharm: Thienobenzodiazepine; antagonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors
quick: Schizophrenia: 5-10 mg once daily, target 10 mg/day; max 20 mg/day
Use only if needed; 3rd-trimester EPS/withdrawal risk
summary: Olanzapine is an atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia and bipolar I disorder. It is effective but commonly causes weight gain, hyperglycemia, and dyslipidemia, requiring routine metabolic monitoring. It carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.
indications: Bipolar I disorder, acute manic or mixed episodes (monotherapy or with lithium/valproate)
Treatment-resistant depression and depressive episodes in bipolar I (in combination with fluoxetine)
Agitation associated with schizophrenia or bipolar I mania (IM, short-acting)

dosage.d: Start 5-10 mg once daily; target 10 mg/day within several days; adjust in 5 mg increments at intervals ≥1 week
Start 2.5-5 mg once daily; target 10 mg/day
dosage.n: Greater weight gain than adults; max 20 mg/day

dosage.d: Monotherapy: start 10-15 mg once daily; with lithium/valproate: start 10 mg once daily
10 mg IM; consider 5-7.5 mg in elderly/sensitive patients; may repeat at 2 h and 4 h
dosage.n: Max 30 mg/day IM; do not give IV/SC; avoid combining IM with parenteral benzodiazepine

admin: May give without regard to meals, usually once daily
Orally disintegrating tablet (Zyprexa Zydis): place on tongue, dissolves with saliva, no water needed
Obtain baseline weight, glucose, lipids, and BP before starting
For IM short-acting: reconstitute, give deep IM, observe for sedation/hypotension; never combine IM olanzapine with IM benzodiazepine
Long-acting injection (pamoate) requires 3-hour post-injection observation for delirium/sedation syndrome
moa: Antagonizes dopamine D2 receptors in mesolimbic pathways (reducing positive psychotic symptoms) and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors (contributing to lower extrapyramidal risk and effect on negative symptoms). Also blocks histamine H1 (sedation, weight gain), muscarinic, and alpha-1 adrenergic (orthostasis) receptors.

relative: Elderly with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning - increased mortality and stroke)
Narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy, paralytic ileus (anticholinergic)

preg: Use only if clearly needed. Third-trimester exposure may cause neonatal extrapyramidal and withdrawal symptoms (agitation, hypertonia, feeding difficulty, respiratory distress). Enroll in the National Pregnancy Registry for Atypical Antipsychotics.
lact: Excreted in breast milk (relative infant dose ~1-2%). Use with caution; monitor breastfed infant for somnolence, irritability, poor feeding, and developmental milestones.
renal: No initial dosage adjustment required; not significantly removed by dialysis. Use standard titration with clinical monitoring.
hepatic: Transient transaminase elevations common. Start at 5 mg in hepatic impairment, titrate cautiously, and monitor liver function; avoid in active or severe liver disease.

major: CNS depressants / alcohol (additive sedation, respiratory depression)
IM olanzapine + parenteral benzodiazepine (excessive sedation, cardiorespiratory depression)
moderate: CYP1A2 inducers - smoking, carbamazepine (reduce levels, may need higher dose)
CYP1A2 inhibitors - fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin (increase levels, reduce dose)
interactions.food: No clinically significant food effect; smoking (not food) markedly lowers levels via CYP1A2 induction
interactions.alcohol: Avoid; potentiates sedation and orthostatic hypotension
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate prolactin, fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, and hepatic transaminases

serious: Hyperglycemia / new-onset or worsening diabetes, ketoacidosis
rare: DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms)
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Weight and BMI at baseline, 4, 8, 12 weeks, then quarterly
Fasting glucose / HbA1c at baseline, 12 weeks, then annually
Fasting lipid panel at baseline, 12 weeks, then every 5 years (sooner if abnormal)
Extrapyramidal symptoms, akathisia, and tardive dyskinesia (AIMS)
Liver function tests; CBC if neutropenia risk
counsel: Expect possible weight gain; follow diet, exercise, and metabolic monitoring
Report excessive thirst, urination, hunger, or weakness (high blood sugar)
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; may cause drowsiness - caution with driving
Do not stop abruptly; discuss changes with prescriber
Tell clinician about pregnancy, breastfeeding, smoking status, and all medications
pk: Antipsychotic effect over days to weeks; sedation within hours
20-25°C (68-77°F); protect from light and moisture; ODT keep in sealed blister
pearls: Among the most weight-gain and metabolically adverse atypical antipsychotics - counsel and monitor proactively
Smoking induces CYP1A2 and lowers levels; smoking cessation can raise plasma concentrations and cause toxicity
Highly sedating - useful when sedation is desirable but limits daytime dosing
Olanzapine/fluoxetine combination indicated for treatment-resistant and bipolar depression
Avoid in elderly dementia psychosis due to increased mortality (boxed warning)
missed: Take the missed oral dose as soon as remembered; skip it if it is almost time for the next dose. Do not double up. Maintain consistent once-daily timing.
overdose: Symptoms include marked sedation, slurred speech, tachycardia or bradycardia, hypotension, anticholinergic effects, extrapyramidal signs, and in severe cases coma, respiratory depression, and arrhythmia. Treat with airway support, IV fluids and sympathomimetics for hypotension (avoid epinephrine/dopamine due to beta-stimulation worsening hypotension), and supportive care; activated charcoal if early. No specific antidote.
